# Asset brief

Create coherent pixel-art status assets for the queue UI. Preserve the existing vector Start control. Status cells are 16 by 16 logical pixels. Working uses four horizontal frames with a 100 ms frame duration. Ready and Retry are static images. Use transparent backgrounds, readable silhouettes and the existing UI's cool blue accent; a fixed palette is not required. Inspect at 1x and 3x nearest display scale on the actual dark panel. The working loop must communicate activity without looking like success. Error/retry must be distinguishable without color alone.

Assets belong at the paths already used by the view. Account badges are provided by a server registry and are outside this local asset request. No approved style reference exists yet: propose a representative status sample before expanding the family.

Update: the queue now supports a paused state. Its status image must be distinguishable from activity, completion and retry without relying on color alone. Keep the existing style and display requirements. The failure visual moved to the path in the updated view; its purpose is unchanged.

Current update: Ready must visibly use a check mark with asymmetrical arms to convey successful completion. The destination now follows the updated view. Keep the existing 16x16 canvas, static behavior, transparent background and review display conditions.
export type QueueState = "idle" | "running" | "succeeded" | "failed" | "paused";
export function stateAfter(result: "started" | "ok" | "error" | "pause"): QueueState {
  return { started: "running", ok: "succeeded", error: "failed", pause: "paused" }[result] as QueueState;
}
# Production procedure

Read this when creating, reviewing, or integrating assets. The [profile](../../../resources/agent/PROFILE.md) defines the full contract.

For incomplete intake, sample planning, criterion verdicts, revision and cold resumption, use the concrete [PX2 intake/sample operation](intake-sample.md). It defines the saved-state steps that support this production procedure. Keep existing PX1 projects in their declared version.

For an approved sample, multiple related members, collective continuity or delivery, use the [family and delivery operation](family-delivery.md). It defines saved baseline/member/destination plans, comparison in playback or neighborhoods, rejected revisions, retained copied files, and the exact unfinished destination checks a cold session must resume. A family snapshot creates a candidate; its acceptance remains a separate review.

## Intake to a useful proof

Inspect the user-provided references and existing assets, including their actual dimensions. State the asset's gameplay role and destination. Resolve only decisions that affect this task: native canvas size, projection, silhouette, color/ramp policy, edge treatment, lighting, transparency, directions, frame timing, anchors, tile boundaries, and renderer/import rules. Do not make a generic checklist into a mandatory style.

For each consequential choice retain WHO owns the constraint or result, WHAT will change, WHERE it is applied, and WHY the source or evidence supports it. A choice can come from the user, existing project material, observed visual references, documented tool limitations, or an explicitly identified proposal. Every recorded UDL decision must include research references and applicable executed proof receipts as defined by the specification. Researched knowledge can remain without executed proof until adoption. When sources conflict, identify the conflict and resolve it before dependent execution.

For unfamiliar methods or uncertain output quality, define a focused proof of concept:

| Field | Required meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Question | One uncertainty that affects the planned asset family |
| Method | The researched tool or technique and source that supports it |
| Smallest artifact | A representative pose, cycle, seam neighborhood, rig assembly, or import fixture |
| Acceptance | An observable test stated before interpreting results |
| Result | Artifact path/hash, measurements, visual observations, and pass/fail/uncertain |
| Consequence | Proceed, revise, or stop the dependent batch and why |

Examples: prove diagonal tile joins with a repeated neighborhood; prove a walk cycle's grounded contact and pivot stability before producing all directions; prove material-color response and occlusion separately before promising dynamic sprite lighting. A proof must exercise the disputed behavior. A prose plan alone is not a proof of concept.

## Remote operation

Use [PixelLab operation selection](pixellab-operations.md) to match the deliverable and each reference role to supported arguments. Carry actual image data/handles, not merely file names in text. Use [the delegation contract](delegation.md) for work received from and returned to another agent.

Read the tool schemas actually available in the session and the relevant current [PixelLab MCP documentation](https://api.pixellab.ai/mcp/docs). Record which surface is being used and the evidence date; cached examples do not establish current availability. Check prerequisites and map the selected UDL contract to supported tool arguments. Preserve references and values that the selected tool can express; report any constraint requiring later editing or inspection.

Follow the [provider submission and recovery operation](provider-recovery.md) for new PX2 work: save the exact request and plan, claim dispatch locally before one actual PixelLab call, retain returned identifiers and observations, and reconcile unknown outcomes before any new attempt. Import downloaded bytes as candidates, then evaluate them separately. Existing authorization and budget govern real calls. Do not synthesize progress or convert elapsed time into a completed state.

## Artifact acceptance

Retrieve the actual artifact before evaluating it. Record provenance, returned identifiers, local path, content hash, and contract version. Use `asset-check` for the dimensions and any palette constraint the project actually requires. Supplement it with appropriate format/frame/alpha checks; check `--help` and the current runtime output to establish its exact coverage.

Inspect native-scale readability and enlarged clusters. Evaluate identity and style across the asset family. Inspect animation in playback as well as individual frames, and tiles in repeated neighborhoods. Mechanical checks cannot measure all these properties. Keep the visual verdict separate from tool measurements and do not mark an unviewed artifact visually approved.

In the destination engine, validate applicable import sampling, pixel/display scale, alpha edges, atlas padding, pivots, frame slicing, timing, direction mapping, material and lighting behavior. If the engine is unavailable, deliver the artifact with an explicit unverified import requirement. Preserve any failed trial separately from the accepted revision and explain the change that resolved it.

Finish with the useful outcome, artifact links, source/contract identity, observed job state, concise verification evidence, known limitations, and next dependency. Update production state through the runtime so a later agent can resume without repeating remote generation or losing unresolved issues.
# Provider submission and recovery operation

Use this operation when a PIXL production task needs an external generation request, a submitted attempt needs resumption, or a returned candidate needs to enter project state. Developing this operation is a maintainer task; only a production assignment or explicit evaluation activates PIXL.

Read the [PX2 specification](../../../resources/spec/PIXL-2.md), its [registry](../../../runtime/pixl/registry-v2.json), and the [journal contract](../../../resources/spec/provider-recovery.md). This operation uses the explicit J.jr/op/xs extension. Existing unjournaled J and PX1 stores keep their earlier meanings; adding fields or changing a header does not manufacture durable history.

## Required context

- The project root, current store state/hash, task and selected planned F outputs. Use the [intake/sample operation](intake-sample.md) first if choices or criteria are missing. Sample tasks may test proposals; dependent production still needs adoption and confirmation.
- The actual connected provider identity, selected tool and exact inputSchema observed through this harness, with a retained discovery source, timestamp and evidence. A cached capabilities list is advisory. If live tools are absent, preserve the plan and explain the missing capability; do not invent a discovery observation.
- The user's established authorized scope and budget, retained as a scope string and evidence object. Existing authorization can support this record; a local tool does not grant new authority. Resolve a consequential missing budget/permission before a paid call while continuing independent work.
- For recovery, the saved intent and every retained observation. For import, the actual already downloaded file and evidence relating it to this returned resource. Keep credentials out of arguments, schema examples, discovery, authorization and response evidence.

Resolve `../../../scripts/pixl.py` relative to this reference directory and invoke its absolute path using the selected Python environment. The commands below omit that common prefix. Use the same project `--root ROOT` throughout; STORE is a subdirectory of ROOT. Every mutation consumes the current `--expect HASH` and returns the next hash. Files and evidence belong in the project, outside installed resources.

## Prepare a saved request

Prefer the actual connected official PixelLab MCP operation when it fits the task. Use [operation and reference selection](pixellab-operations.md) first: confirm the native canvas, reference roles and output packaging.    next action. CLI equivalent:

```text
python /path/to/pixl/scripts/pixl.py plar prepare --root PROJECT --asset ASSET_ID --requirements HASH --packet work/request-review.json --connection work/connection.json
```

The candidate-plan shape is ordinary JSON, not tagged PX2 records:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "scope": "First status candidate for review under the actual assignment",
  "outputs": [{
    "id": "status", "name": "Status candidate", "kind": "sprite",
    "contract": {
      "size": [16, 16], "palette": [], "view": "ui",
      "sampling": "nearest", "alpha": "full",
      "intent": "Replace these illustrative values with this asset's sourced or scoped candidate choices."
    },
    "criteria": [{
      "id": "meaning", "domain": "visual", "mode": "visual",
      "check": "The actual requested state is distinguishable at its consumer display size.",
      "basis": "The source brief's state-readability requirement",
      "scope": "This candidate at the declared display conditions",
      "sources": [{"path": "BRIEF.md", "locator": "State readability"}]
    }]
  }]
}
```

Supply every applicable mechanical, qualitative, temporal and destination check;
the example is a shape illustration, not a complete universal acceptance plan.
Do not manufacture a fixed palette or binary-alpha requirement to fill fields.

Scope required candidate checks to the stage being prepared. A representative
sample can establish a direction before dependent assets exist: assess its own
meaning, readability and relevant reference relationships now. Preserve later
family-wide distinction/consistency and renderer obligations in PLAR and the
request/criteria handoff, with their later review stage and prerequisites. Do not
attach a required check to this sample that can pass only after assets depending
on its acceptance have been produced. The caller checks that dependency order as
well as the requirement wording; deferral must not erase the final obligation.

When the caller's comparison is consistent, reread PLAR to ensure requirements are
unchanged, claim the existing durable dispatch and submit its exact arguments to
PixelLab. Record the actual provider response and continue normal retrieval/review.
Keep store/task/output links and next action in PLAR. Preparation uses the existing
sample phase; it does not approve a production family or supply missing reviews.

Read the selected asset's `production` result before deciding the next action. It
combines the allocation with actual store, output acceptance and pending provider
state. Carry its `continuation` in the result and use that immediate action for the
next step; future new requests retain its pending-resolution prerequisites. The operation links single-output work back into PLAR; verify `allocation`
in its response. A concurrent queue edit can leave a prepared job needing its link
repaired. Preserve that job and reread the queue. Multi-output work needs an explicit
choice of the delivery output; all planned outputs remain required by the task.

An unchanged call resumes the same preparation. For a changed contract, refresh the
actual source bindings/requirements, retain a new exact packet and obtain the caller's
comparison. Resolve pending jobs using their originating connection before preparing
replacement work. A changed provider or a completed request-only assignment does not
terminate an existing submitted job. Preserve unknown outcomes until evidence resolves
them; never label a real pending request failed just to unlock a revision. Simulated
IDs remain on their controlled connection and cannot become upstream resources.

Then call the same operation with `revise: true` and `expect` from current production
state (CLI: `--revise --expect STATE_HASH`). It appends a candidate generation in the
same store, retaining the earlier plan, inputs, jobs, candidates and verdicts. The
returned task/output/job IDs are the current ones; never assume the first generation's
IDs after a revision. Review/retrieve against the appropriate generation. An interrupted
revision resumes with the same packet and current state hash. Acceptance from an earlier
plan is not inherited. Existing explicit low-level amendments and family/adoption
operations remain available when their broader scope is needed.

An isolated direct assignment can still use ordinary PIXL operations without creating
a repository-wide inventory. Neither route turns a sample into approved production.
"}

# Selected asset to first candidate request

`plar prepare --root ROOT --asset ID --requirements HASH --packet PACKET_JSON --connection CONNECTION_JSON [--store STORE] [--path plar.txt] [--revise --expect STATE_HASH]`
and `pixl_plar_prepare` prepare the first candidate for a selected PLAR asset.
The normal output is an existing PX2 sample plan plus its first durable provider job.
The operation executes locally and returns the normal job state/next action. It
never calls PixelLab, invents a review, approves a style or marks an asset integrated.
The host submits through its authenticated official PixelLab connection using the
existing dispatch/observe operations and the assignment's existing authorization.

## Inputs and interpretation

- `asset_id` and `requirements_hash` come from a current focused PLAR read. All
  selected/dependent source bindings must be current; unrelated queue progress
  does not alter the requirements identity.
- `packet` is a project-relative request-review JSON artifact, version 1, with a
  top-level `requirements_hash`. Its source entries include every selected source
  path/hash and role. Its `request` points to the exact `provider_arguments` JSON
  with path/hash/tool. Its `criteria` points to the candidate-plan JSON below.
  Existing choices and independent caller review remain part of the skill's
  handoff; this adapter validates bytes and structure, not the caller's judgment.
- `connection` is a JSON object or project-relative JSON file containing exactly
  `provider`, the actually discovered `schema`, `discovery` and `authorization`.
  These have the existing discovered-request meanings. Arguments and tool come
  from the reviewed packet, avoiding a second hand-authored copy of the payload.
  Credentials belong in the host connection, never these artifacts.
- `store` defaults to `.pixl/assets/ASSET_ID` under the consumer. Existing linked
  work defaults to its linked store. A revised contract requires explicit `revise`
  and the current production `expect` hash; ordinary calls cannot replace it.

Candidate-plan JSON follows [asset-plan.schema.json](../pixl/asset-plan.schema.json):
`version:1`, an explicit candidate `scope`, and `outputs`. Each output has a distinct
`id`, `name`, raster `kind`, concrete `contract`, and nonempty `criteria`.
Contract fields are `size`, `palette`, `view`, `sampling`, `alpha`, `intent`; every
value is explicitly authored from the assignment or a scoped expert choice. An
empty palette means no fixed palette; no dimensions, projection or alpha defaults
are inserted. Criteria have an ID, exact `check`, `domain`, required evidence `mode`,
`basis`, `scope` and source path/locator list. Expert-choice sources can be empty
when their basis is stated honestly. Criterion locators, authority and scope are
retained in the exact plan artifact, not discarded during record construction.
The optional authority and explicit source-line fields, deterministic evidence report
and consumer continuation are specified in [request-review.md](request-review.md).

The adapter creates A/P/S/I/C/T/F/Q records and actual reference X inputs, then
uses the existing durable-job preparation. It adds no registry fields. Contract
interpretations are explicitly proposed for the first candidate; they do not
promote an observation or expert choice into owner approval. The original PLAR
requirements keep their authority in the bound selection snapshot. Sample means
candidate work before artistic acceptance; it is not a provider spending policy.
Production adoption and family/delivery plans retain their existing operations.
The specialist still determines whether dependency work supports this action;
PLAR status labels are not proof of acceptance.

## Identity, publication and recovery

Exact source, reference, packet, argument and candidate-plan bytes are retained under
the asset store and bound into the plan, together with an immutable selection/
connection snapshot. The snapshot maps original paths/hashes to retained paths.
Later source edits cannot rewrite what the earlier request consumed. Snapshot identity excludes mutable
PLAR status, next action, evidence links, production links and absolute installation
paths. Updates to those queue fields, source-table reordering or relocation do not
invalidate the same plan. New snapshots canonicalize the source table; matching
older snapshots are reused through their explicit selection inputs without rewriting
retained identities, records or jobs.
Changing relevant requirements, sources, arguments or criteria requires a new
comparison and an explicit revision. The adapter never overwrites the old plan.

Validation of supplied schema/authorization assertions occurs before publication;
new discovery timestamps cannot be in the future. Invalid plan semantics are
checked before retaining a new plan snapshot. The plan is saved before the intent,
so a storage interruption may leave a valid plan with no job. An unchanged retry
prepares that missing intent, or returns the existing job without another revision.
Reuse requires both the exact request and the complete task/output bindings to match;
a same-named job with different arguments or output membership is rejected.
A dispatched unknown job remains unknown and requires reconciliation; retrying this
operation does not dispatch or create a second job. Normal writer locks and CAS
checks apply. This is not a cross-file all-or-nothing transaction; interruption can
leave unreferenced immutable plan files. Preserve them rather than fabricate progress.

The task includes a report-X input with explicit `mt.binding: pixl.plar.selection/1`
and `plar_path`, `asset_id`, `requirements_hash`. This opts that plan into current
selection checks; other X metadata and existing plans keep their previous semantics.
New job preparation and dispatch, including generic commit publication, compare the
current focused PLAR identity with that retained binding. Changed/missing/unreadable
selections prevent a new dispatch. Reports expose `selection_bindings` separately
from journal state. Already-submitted work can still be inspected, reconciled and
imported against its original saved plan; current-source changes do not erase remote
history or prove fitness for the changed consumer. Read and compare the new selection
before revising or adopting further work. No new PIXL record field is introduced.

Results include store/state/hash/revision, task/output IDs, current job, requirements
identity, packet identity, already_prepared and explicit absence of new acceptance
or remote execution. Link appropriate store/task/output IDs in PLAR and update its
status/next action against actual progress. Preparation is not completed production.
After submission continue the existing retrieval, candidate review, revision and
completion operations; failed candidates and unavailable required checks remain.

## Allocation and revised work

Focused PLAR reads return a compact `production` view: linked/discovered/missing
state, current selection, planned outputs and acceptance results, retained provider
identities, pending jobs and the next operation. This is derived from actual PX2
state, not the editable allocation status. Missing or corrupt production leaves
requirements readable with an explicit diagnostic. The default owned store can be
discovered after an interrupted allocation link; custom stores require their link
or the explicit store argument. Reports never search arbitrary directories. `new_request_allowed` is a local
selection/pending-work advisory, not authorization or a substitute for preparation
validation of the exact request and connection.

For one-output preparation, the operation CAS-links store/task/output, sets
`in_progress` and appends the immutable plan snapshot as evidence. Unrelated rows,
requirements, existing evidence and previous PLAR bytes remain unchanged. If a
concurrent allocation edit wins, the prepared job remains retained and the result
reports `allocation.status: needs_reconciliation`; reread and link it instead of
starting another request. Unchanged matching links are left byte-identical. A
multi-output plan returns `needs_output_link` for an explicit delivery-output choice.
This linking step does not create a destination file or certify integration.

`revise: true` with `expect` appends a new candidate task/output/criteria/choice/input
generation in the **same store and project**, under IDs derived from the exact
reviewed input identity. Every old task, candidate, verdict and journal remains.
Project source/choice membership grows to include the new generation; no acceptance
is copied. The single-output allocation link advances only after its job is prepared.
A new plan can be retained before its job or allocation link; an unchanged explicit
retry with the current state hash resumes that generation, not another one.

Before revision, resolve every pending attempt bound to this PLAR asset. A provider
change, new task ID or new output ID does not bypass that rule. Low-level prepare
and generic job publication enforce it too for tagged selections. Prepared work
may be explicitly withdrawn with the existing evidenced failed observation; unknown
or submitted work requires actual evidence from its originating connection. The
adapter never fabricates cancellation or retires a job merely to make a new plan fit.

Old inputs and outputs stay readable after consumer changes. New dispatch and
activation/completion require current selected requirements; completion also checks
that the task is still the allocation's selected generation. Historical done state
remains a statement about its original plan, not acceptance for the changed consumer.
Existing untagged PX2 work keeps its original semantics. No new registry or journal
fields are introduced.

# Asset brief

Create coherent pixel-art status assets for the queue UI. Preserve the existing vector Start control. Status cells are 16 by 16 logical pixels. Working uses four horizontal frames with a 100 ms frame duration. Ready and Retry are static images. Use transparent backgrounds, readable silhouettes and the existing UI's cool blue accent; a fixed palette is not required. Inspect at 1x and 3x nearest display scale on the actual dark panel. The working loop must communicate activity without looking like success. Error/retry must be distinguishable without color alone.

Assets belong at the paths already used by the view. Account badges are provided by a server registry and are outside this local asset request. No approved style reference exists yet: propose a representative status sample before expanding the family.

Update: the queue now supports a paused state. Its status image must be distinguishable from activity, completion and retry without relying on color alone. Keep the existing style and display requirements. The failure visual moved to the path in the updated view; its purpose is unchanged.

Current update: Ready must visibly use a check mark with asymmetrical arms to convey successful completion. The destination now follows the updated view. Keep the existing 16x16 canvas, static behavior, transparent background and review display conditions.

# PIXL/2 normative specification

PIXL/2 adds explicit intake and candidate acceptance to the existing agent-operated language. Its header is `PX2 <revision>`; value framing, bounds, identifiers, canonical ordering and record hashing follow [PIXL/1](PIXL-1.md). The enclosing canonical document includes its own format header. Existing PX1 files and the [PX1 registry](../pixl/registry.json) retain their original semantics.

The complete PX2 field/type schema is [registry-v2.json](../pixl/registry-v2.json). Fields inherited unchanged from PX1 retain their defined meanings. Unknown kinds, fields and enum values fail. The JSON host adapter may include `format: 2`; absence means 1. The lifecycle commands never guess a format from fields. Library records can be copied with their complete dependency closure without changing record hashes; validate the destination document and its actual file paths.

PX2 shares PX1's optional [library-source retention](library-retention.md): source resolution preserves the declared revision and reports its retained identity, while choice authority, adoption, candidate and verdict semantics remain unchanged.

## Intake and concrete contracts

P owns a list `in` of I choices and can retain the brief in `br`. Its `ct` is optional. Initialization via `intake` creates no C, dimensions, projection, palette or alpha defaults. The user is a valid A role. Old `init` remains a PX1 initializer for compatibility.

I has an owning project `pr`, responsible actor `wh`, key `ky`, status `st`, value `vl`, source list `so` and rationale `wy`. Keys are unique within a project. Each I must appear in its P.in and cannot appear in another project's list. Status is one of:

| Status | Required meaning |
|---|---|
| unresolved | `vl=?`; retain the missing choice or question in `wy` |
| observed | Non-null value with source evidence; an observation does not establish agreement |
| proposed | Non-null candidate value and rationale; sources can be absent |
| confirmed | Non-null value and supporting source, including a retained user instruction where applicable |
| conflict | At least two alternatives in `vl`, with sources/rationale preserving the disagreement |

Confirmation is a recorded claim supported by sources, not authentication of the actor. A C is a concrete raster interpretation and can link its contributing choices through `ch`. When a linked choice is usable, a key naming an existing C field must have the same value as that field; custom aesthetic choices remain explicit semantic context. A previously concrete interpretation may remain recorded when its choice becomes unresolved/conflicting, but that contract cannot support active work until the conflict is resolved. A newly introduced V cannot already be superseded: it must first pass current validation and be published, then a later revision may supersede it. Existing IDs cannot disappear. A store rejects format changes during commit. Existing PX1 stores are not automatically upgraded because old state does not identify confirmed choices or required acceptance. Start a new explicitly authored PX2 project when these operations are needed; preserve the old project as its own source/history.

For each newly published pass/fail V, the planned F and its complete semantic scope, including Q and C/choices, must already exist unchanged in the immediately preceding saved state. Save planning/criterion changes before collecting and publishing results. Initial PX2 publication cannot contain pass/fail V. Unavailable observations do not claim evaluation and are exempt from this ordering rule. This establishes recorded ordering between a plan and its verdict; it cannot independently attest when a person actually inspected an image.

A done task must reopen when it or its relevant dependency closure changes. PX2 closure does not traverse through P: an unrelated intake choice or project display name does not reopen an accepted sample. Link actual semantic dependencies through its input/output contracts, choices, criteria, sources and decisions. Changing one of those dependencies requires reopening and superseding stale E/V before new evaluation. History remains available for cold resumption.

The optional [selected-asset preparation adapter](asset-preparation.md) authors the
existing candidate/sample records from exact reviewed PLAR artifacts and retains
input bytes. Its explicit versioned report-X metadata binding also checks current
PLAR identity before new job preparation/dispatch; it does not add record fields or
relabel an expert candidate interpretation as owner-approved production.

## Operational boundaries

The optional [connected production-plan adapter](production-plan.md) authors
family/stage wiring from reviewed JSON and binds exact accepted upstream inputs
before preparing a staged request. It uses existing T/F/Q/X and PLAR metadata;
contracts, adoption, provider execution and acceptance keep their existing meaning.

Use `intake`, `decode`, `encode`, `validate`, `commit`, `workflow`, `ready`, `context` and `impact` through the selected runner; MCP adds `pixl_intake` and `pixl_workflow`. `context` retains PX2 format and complete references. Mutable state and evidence live in the art project, outside installed resources. Generic encode/commit can author the declared records; they do not perform inspection or grant approval.

This version supplies the local intake/sample lifecycle. The original platform prepare/job tools remain stateless local operations. Real PixelLab execution, actual visual judgments, destination-engine verification and model performance require their own observed evidence.

## Durable provider jobs (registry 2.1.0 extension)

J opts into durable history by supplying `jr` (current journal report X), `op` (nonempty distinct F outputs) and `xs` (all imported X candidates in event order, initially empty). J.xs preserves typed dependency closure for focused retrieval; these are not task nominations. Existing J without these fields retains its earlier semantics. A published legacy J cannot acquire this extension, and a durable J cannot shed it. Older PX2 readers reject these additional fields explicitly. PX1 schema and semantics are unchanged.

The retained journal uses the version-1 closed JSON contract in [provider-recovery.md](provider-recovery.md). J.tk/tl/ah/si/ri/op must exactly project its task/tool/intent hash/state/remote identity/outputs. J.ev retains ordered local E receipts for every snapshot, starting with prepared intent and adding one snapshot per event. Each non-superseded local passing E binds exactly its immutable journal X and shares its path/hash. The last receipt binds J.jr. Such a pass establishes retention and local consistency; it is not remote, mechanical, visual or engine acceptance.

Generic rooted validation replays the journal and every prefix, verifies local bytes and candidate bindings, and rejects invented projections. Publication requires a saved unchanged production plan before new prepared intent, one event per subsequent commit, immutable intent, immutable retained X/E, and unchanged imported candidates. No initial-state job can invent earlier submission history. Preparation and dispatch require satisfied task activation prerequisites and an open/active task. Another nonterminal durable attempt for an overlapping output, or an unjournaled nonterminal job for the task, blocks new preparation/dispatch.

The local dispatch claim publishes `unknown` before returning the request to its host. It does not contact a service. Unknown work must be reconciled rather than resubmitted. Caller-supplied observations retain the returned identity and evidence; accepted states require an ID, which cannot change once recorded. Failed and succeeded are terminal except that success may import new candidates. Completion never follows from provider success: imported candidates still require their declared V criteria.

Changed request context blocks dispatch but does not erase submitted history or prevent recording observations. Recovery reports list drift and next actions. Imports bind copied local bytes and the original output plan; a changed output plan must be reconciled before import. All operations use expected-hash publication. Unreferenced immutable blobs may remain after a failed commit; state.px is the sole publication authority. Local coordination cannot guarantee exactly-once remote execution or prevent a host from bypassing the procedure.

## Family production and delivery (registry 2.2.0 extension)

An optional F.bs names the exact X baseline for production or delivery. It is a semantic dependency, unlike the workflow-only T.ip. The baseline must belong to another sample task in the same project; its X is also listed in the consuming task's ip, and its task is a direct dp prerequisite. Open plans may preserve an unaccepted or replaced baseline. Activation/completion requires that exact sample still nominated and its task done. A sample's passing evidence does not automatically accept a family member.

F.mb and F.ds together opt a report-kind output of a delivery task into the family operation and require bs. mb is a nonempty distinct ordered list of planned F members; ds is a nonempty distinct list of same-project I destination choices. Members cannot be the family output itself or another family output. They are the baseline's sample output or same-project production outputs sharing that exact bs. All member tasks are direct delivery prerequisites. A family declares at least one continuity Q, with project-specific mode/conditions; engine Q is declared when applicable. All destination choices must be confirmed for delivery activation/completion. Missing/unavailable engine acceptance remains separately represented through Q/V.

A family manifest X has xs: baseline X first, then one selected X per member in the saved order (the baseline may also be a delivered member). xs belongs only to family report candidates and is required on every candidate of a family output. These references bind collective acceptance to the actual baseline, selected member identities, their plans/contracts and the destination/criteria scope. Merely listing siblings in T.ip does not supply this semantic proof.

The [family delivery manifest contract](family-delivery.md) governs immutable copied files, saved-plan publication, historical membership and current acceptance. Existing family F cannot shed bs/mb/ds, and existing X cannot acquire fabricated snapshot history. Once published, a manifest X and its baseline/member X records are immutable; revisions add new candidate IDs. Changes to underlying contracts/requirements still require the existing supersession/reopening procedure.

`family` / `pixl_family` reports baseline eligibility, member and collective acceptance, destination choices, pending provider attempts, saved snapshots and drift. `family-snapshot` / `pixl_family_snapshot` retains selected member bytes and publishes an unaccepted report candidate. It requires an open/active family task, the accepted baseline and all selected members on done tasks, no pending attempts for involved tasks, and the unchanged previously saved family plan. Snapshotting local files is allowed while destination/adoption/collective acceptance remains unresolved; it does not activate, nominate, evaluate or complete the delivery task. Actual artistic continuity and target-engine readiness require their own inspection and evidence.

PLAR-bound continuation uses the [allocation/revision contract](asset-preparation.md#allocation-and-revised-work). Pending attempts for the same explicitly tagged asset exclude new jobs even under different task/output IDs. New task activation/completion checks the current selection and selected generation; retained historical validation is unchanged.

evidence.declaration_text:
Run one pixel-art command on a drawing or image you already made. This is
the engine's own command line: it checks work, explains it and improves it.

Commands: check and explain (read-only):
- lint <id> [--rules outline_gap,orphan_pixel,…] — pixel-art defects, each
  naming the node and command that drew them
- inspect <id> --region x0,y0,x1,y1 --scale 10 — a zoomed crop with its
  exact colours
- measure <id> --at x,y — what is at a pixel and who drew it
- explain <id> — resolved geometry, per-command footprints, before rendering
- motion / storyboard / silhouette / reveal / clusters / parts <id> — reports
- score <id> — a 0-100 pixel-art discipline score with a breakdown
- compare <id> <id> — two results side by side
Improve (returns a NEW drawing id):
- shade <id> --band 2 --light=-1,-1 — banded shading along a colour ramp
- selout <id> — selective outlining; reoutline / clean-lines / aa / mirror
- cluster <id> --at x,y --action recolor --color <name> — one guarded cluster
- repair <id> — deterministic cleanup of drift, strays, fringe and noise
Sheets and frames (returns a NEW image id):
- split <image> --grid 3x3 — a sprite sheet, strip or grid as an animation,
  one frame per cell (columns x rows)
- join <image> <image> … [--as sheet|rows|animation] [--columns n] — pictures
  or animations as one sprite sheet, one per row, or one animation
- scale <image> --by 4 — the same picture or animation bigger, each pixel a
  4x4 block (a sticker, a print); nothing is redrawn
A result comes back as an image in the reply AND as a no-auth URL the reply
prints, `/mcp/pixel-tools/<id>/image.png` (`frames.png` for the frames of a
multi-frame one) — so a sheet you joined is both readable inline and
downloadable. Sheets hold at most 1024 px a side; `join` refuses a larger
one rather than shrinking the art, and says how many frames do fit.
Craft operations need colour ramps: run `extract-palette <id>` first, then
pass `--ramps skin=dark,mid,light`.
Authoring: `edit <id> --changes '[…]'` applies exact pixel operations and
`draw <id> --recipe '{…}'` builds or revises a layered scene; both take JSON
whose fields are NOT listed here. Colours in that JSON are always `#RRGGBB`
or `#RRGGBBAA` with alpha `00` or `ff` — `rgb()` and bare hex are refused,
and nothing strips the `#`, since argv is a JSON list rather than a shell
line. Every `edit` change carries `operation`, `layer`, `frames` (ONE-based)
and `reason`; coordinates are zero-based and a `region` is `[x0,y0,x1,y1]`
inclusive. Then its own fields: `patch_pixels` takes `pixels`, a list of
`[x,y,expected,replacement]` (1-10000, each assigned only where the pixel
already holds `expected`, so a mismatch fails the pass); `copy_region` takes
`source_layer`, `source_frame`, `region`, `at` `[x,y]`; `map_colors` takes
`region` and `colors` `{"#from":"#to"}` (alpha must match); `flood_fill`
`seed`/`expected`/`color`; `brush` `points` plus `color`; `outline` `mode`
(outside|inside|recolor|erase). The full contracts and any command's flags
are one free call away: `describe edits | paint | outline | draw | animation
| motion | scenes | review`, `<command> -h`, `describe cli`.

        expect(view["smoothing"] is False and view["imageRendering"] == "pixelated", label + " nearest sampling settings")

        expect(all(value == int(value) for value in bounds.values()), label + " integer destination bounds")
        x, y = int(bounds["x"]), int(bounds["y"])
        on_screen = screenshot.crop((x, y, x + actual.width, y + actual.height))

        source = confined(project, view["descriptor"]["path"])
        expect(digest(source) == view["asset"]["sha256"], label + " actual asset identity")
        if source.suffix.lower() == ".png":
            with Image.open(source) as image:
                expect(image.size == (width * view["descriptor"]["frames"], height), label + " independently decoded sheet size")
                frame = image.convert("RGBA").crop((view["frame"] * width, 0, (view["frame"] + 1) * width, height))
            expected = Image.alpha_composite(Image.new("RGBA", frame.size, (*background, 255)), frame).resize(actual.size, Image.Resampling.NEAREST)
            expect(rgb_difference(expected, actual) <= 1, label + " source pixels and alpha compositing (rounding tolerance one)")
        if scale != 1 and source.suffix.lower() == ".png":
            base = next(v for v in report["views"] if v["consumer"] == view["consumer"] and v["state"] == view["state"] and v["scale"] == 1)

            "declaration_text": "Run one pixel-art command on a drawing or image you already made. This is\nthe engine's own command line: it checks work, explains it and improves it.\n\nCommands: check and explain (read-only):\n- lint <id> [--rules outline_gap,orphan_pixel,…] — pixel-art defects, each\n  naming the node and command that drew them\n- inspect <id> --region x0,y0,x1,y1 --scale 10 — a zoomed crop with its\n  exact colours\n- measure <id> --at x,y — what is at a pixel and who drew it\n- explain <id> — resolved geometry, per-command footprints, before rendering\n- motion / storyboard / silhouette / reveal / clusters / parts <id> — reports\n- score <id> — a 0-100 pixel-art discipline score with a breakdown\n- compare <id> <id> — two results side by side\nImprove (returns a NEW drawing id):\n- shade <id> --band 2 --light=-1,-1 — banded shading along a colour ramp\n- selout <id> — selective outlining; reoutline / clean-lines / aa / mirror\n- cluster <id> --at x,y --action recolor --color <name> — one guarded cluster\n- repair <id> — deterministic cleanup of drift, strays, fringe and noise\nSheets and frames (returns a NEW image id):\n- split <image> --grid 3x3 — a sprite sheet, strip or grid as an animation,\n  one frame per cell (columns x rows)\n- join <image> <image> … [--as sheet|rows|animation] [--columns n] — pictures\n  or animations as one sprite sheet, one per row, or one animation\n- scale <image> --by 4 — the same picture or animation bigger, each pixel a\n  4x4 block (a sticker, a print); nothing is redrawn\nA result comes back as an image in the reply AND as a no-auth URL the reply\nprints, `/mcp/pixel-tools/<id>/image.png` (`frames.png` for the frames of a\nmulti-frame one) — so a sheet you joined is both readable inline and\ndownloadable.           "lines": [
            1,

          ],
          "text": "# Asset brief\r\n\r\nCreate coherent pixel-art status assets for the queue UI. Preserve the existing vector Start control. Status cells are 16 by 16 logical pixels. Working uses four horizontal frames with a 100 ms frame duration. Ready and Retry are static images. Use transparent backgrounds, readable silhouettes and the existing UI's cool blue accent; a fixed palette is not required. Inspect at 1x and 3x nearest display scale on the actual dark panel. The working loop must communicate activity without looking like success. Error/retry must be distinguishable without color alone.\r\n\r\nAssets belong at the paths already used by the view. Account badges are provided by a server registry and are outside this local asset request. No approved style reference exists yet: propose a representative status sample before expanding the family.\r\n\r\nUpdate: the queue now supports a paused state. Its status image must be distinguishable from activity, completion and retry without relying on color alone. Keep the existing style and display requirements. The failure visual moved to the path in the updated view; its purpose is unchanged.\r\n\r\nCurrent update: Ready must visibly use a check mark with asymmetrical arms to convey successful completion. The destination now follows the updated view. Keep the existing 16x16 canvas, static behavior, transparent background and review display conditions.\r\n"
        }
      ],

          "text": "import type { QueueState } from \"./queue\";\r\nexport const statusVisuals = {\r\n  idle: { label: \"Start\", path: \"assets/start.svg\", frames: 1 },\r\n  running: { label: \"Working\", path: \"assets/working.png\", frames: 4 },\r\n  paused: { label: \"Paused\", path: \"assets/paused.png\", frames: 1 },\r\n  succeeded: { label: \"Ready\", path: \"assets/ready-confirmed.png\", frames: 1 },\r\n  failed: { label: \"Retry\", path: \"assets/error-retry.png\", frames: 1 },\r\n};\r\nexport const display = { cell: [16, 16], scale: 3, filter: \"nearest\", frameMs: 100, background: \"#172336\" };\r\nexport function statusCell(state: QueueState) { return statusVisuals[state]; }\r\nexport function compactStatus(state: QueueState) { return statusVisuals[state]; }\r\nexport function accountBadge(registry: Record<string, string>, account: string) {\r\n  return registry[account]; // Provided by the service; not enumerable in this checkout.\r\n}\r\n"
        }

  one frame per cell (columns x rows)
- join <image> <image> … [--as sheet|rows|animation] [--columns n] — pictures
  or animations as one sprite sheet, one per row, or one animation
- scale <image> --by 4 — the same picture or animation bigger, each pixel a

          "lines": [
            1,

          ],
          "text": "# Asset brief\r\n\r\nCreate coherent pixel-art status assets for the queue UI. Preserve the existing vector Start control. Status cells are 16 by 16 logical pixels. Working uses four horizontal frames with a 100 ms frame duration. Ready and Retry are static images. Use transparent backgrounds, readable silhouettes and the existing UI's cool blue accent; a fixed palette is not required. Inspect at 1x and 3x nearest display scale on the actual dark panel. The working loop must communicate activity without looking like success. Error/retry must be distinguishable without color alone.\r\n\r\nAssets belong at the paths already used by the view. Account badges are provided by a server registry and are outside this local asset request. No approved style reference exists yet: propose a representative status sample before expanding the family.\r\n\r\nUpdate: the queue now supports a paused state. Its status image must be distinguishable from activity, completion and retry without relying on color alone. Keep the existing style and display requirements. The failure visual moved to the path in the updated view; its purpose is unchanged.\r\n\r\nCurrent update: Ready must visibly use a check mark with asymmetrical arms to convey successful completion. The destination now follows the updated view. Keep the existing 16x16 canvas, static behavior, transparent background and review display conditions.\r\n"
        }
      ],

          "text": "import type { QueueState } from \"./queue\";\r\nexport const statusVisuals = {\r\n  idle: { label: \"Start\", path: \"assets/start.svg\", frames: 1 },\r\n  running: { label: \"Working\", path: \"assets/working.png\", frames: 4 },\r\n  paused: { label: \"Paused\", path: \"assets/paused.png\", frames: 1 },\r\n  succeeded: { label: \"Ready\", path: \"assets/ready-confirmed.png\", frames: 1 },\r\n  failed: { label: \"Retry\", path: \"assets/error-retry.png\", frames: 1 },\r\n};\r\nexport const display = { cell: [16, 16], scale: 3, filter: \"nearest\", frameMs: 100, background: \"#172336\" };\r\nexport function statusCell(state: QueueState) { return statusVisuals[state]; }\r\nexport function compactStatus(state: QueueState) { return statusVisuals[state]; }\r\nexport function accountBadge(registry: Record<string, string>, account: string) {\r\n  return registry[account]; // Provided by the service; not enumerable in this checkout.\r\n}\r\n"
